title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28: sales were 96 vs baseline 96.5 (x0.995). No prior price increase at this level. Past promotions show x2.09 lift at 30% discount; reverse not observed. Use x0.96 multiplier (4% downside) with low confidence.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.5. A 4.5% price increase to $10.32 from $9.88 is a known demand-lowering driver. Past promotions show price elasticity: 30% off drove x2.09 (noise-adjusted) lifts, but no data exists for price increases. The 2026-09-28 week had the same price ($10.32) and sold 96 units (vs baseline 96.5), a neutral effect. No event, promotion, or post-promo dip is scheduled. The classical model's 1.00 multiplier is correct for no known promotion, but ignores the price effect. With only one prior price test at this level and no observed drop, evidence is thin. Shrink toward 1.0. The price increase is a downside driver with low confidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.5 | 5%-95%: 62.6 - 233.8 | 10%-90%: 67.2 - 191.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
